events.reasoning: The code fulfills all task requirements. It reads CHECKS_FILE and ignores empty lines, executes each command via subprocess with shell=True from the current working directory, captures stdout and stderr, and continues regardless of exit status. It writes an HTML report starting with `<!DOCTYPE html>`, containing `<title>Command Report</title>`, a single `<table>` with the required header row, and one row per command with the command in the first cell and a `<pre>` containing stdout followed by stderr in the second cell. It appends `START <command>` and `END <command> exit=<code>` lines to LOG_FILE, handles the start-failure case with an `ERROR` line and puts the message in the report's `<pre>`, prints the required error to stderr and exits 1 if CHECKS_FILE can't be read, and prints `Report written to <REPORT_FILE>` to stdout. The example scenario (alpha command and false) produces the expected two table rows and START/END log lines. Minor details like using `.strip()` instead of only stripping newlines do not affect functional correctness for typical inputs.

findings.message: Consider possible security implications associated with the subprocess module.
subprocess call with shell=True identified, security issue.

Found 'subprocess' function 'run' with 'shell=True'. This is dangerous because this call will spawn the command using a shell process. Doing so propagates current shell settings and variables, which makes it much easier for a malicious actor to execute commands. Use 'shell=False' instead.
